LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION- • COMMAS • DOUBLE QUOTATION MARKS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation- • Commas • Double Quotation Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation- • Commas • Double Quotation Marks, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Which punctuation marks do you know? 2. Why do we punctuate sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation- • Commas • Double Quotation Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation- • Commas • Double Quotation Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. advocate the use of correct punctuation in written communication. Learner is guided to: • Read a short text and identify punctuation marks used collaboratively with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could be given more considerable time. • Use commas to show pauses between words, phrases or clauses. • Complete sentences using double quotation marks and commas. • Pick out sentences with double quotation marks in newspapers, magazines, articles or internet resources. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital resources with appropriate accessibility features or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to use the digital devices. 1. Which punctuation marks do you know? 2. Why do we punctuate sentences? 63 • Play punctuation games with peers. Assign roles based on functional ability of the learner. • Create posters or charts with sentences with double quotation marks and commas and display them in class, . Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to create the charts and posters. Core Competence developed: Digital literacy is developed as the learner explores internet resources on the use of the comma and double punctuation marks.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation- • Commas • Double Quotation Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
